message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by collecting cards from opponents when you finish your own hand. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise your turn ends. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you have one card left, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The first player to discard all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in each opponent’s hand:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two / Reverse / Skip = 20 points.
• Wild / Wild Draw Four = 50 points.
Points are added to the winner’s total. | | **Game end** | The first player to reach the agreed‑upon score (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional house rules** - *Stacking*: Some players allow stacking of Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards (the next player must match or draw). - *No “Wild Draw Four” cheat*: A player may challenge a Wild Draw Four play; if the challenger has a matching color, the challenger draws four cards instead. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak or add house rules to suit your group.
